finding: ATM_TASK_SCOPE_EXPANSION_REQUIRED exists nowhere in packages/ or scripts/ except the assertion that still requires it, and it is absent from docs/governance/error-code-registry.json. Its throw carried the message 'Task X has staged or modified deliverable-like files outside targetWork.allowedFiles; update the task scope/deliverables instead of editing runtime locks', i.e. a claim-time refusal when out-of-scope deliverable-like files are already staged. git log -S locates the removal around ae5fc3e5a (TASK-ERR-0010). The code was therefore retired from source while its fixture kept asserting it and the canonical registry was never updated, which is exactly the treatment the ErrorCode contract forbids: any ATM_* addition, rename or retirement must go through the shared ErrorCode route and the canonical registry, with emitter, generator, schema, docs/ERROR_CODES.md and focused tests updated together.
expectedBehavior: Either the claim-time scope-expansion refusal still exists and must be reachable under a registered code, or it was deliberately superseded by the direction-lock and work-admission mechanisms that now enforce scope at edit and commit time, in which case the retirement must be recorded in the canonical registry and the fixture rewritten to assert whichever code now owns the behaviour. What must not stand is the current state: a protection asserted by a validator, absent from the code, and unknown to the registry, so nobody can tell whether it was replaced or simply lost.
evidenceOrRepro: node --strip-types scripts/validate-task-direction-governance.ts --mode validate at HEAD c486a50413c7ea3865adf218d69bb9550431b607 fails at adopter-core.ts:325. The assertion was made self-diagnosing before being read and reports 'observed: <no error thrown>' — next --claim completes normally with a file staged at atomic_workbench/atomization-coverage/exclusion-inventory.json while the task allowedFiles contain only src/one.ts. grep for the code across packages/ and scripts/ returns only that fixture; grep against docs/governance/error-code-registry.json returns zero.
followUp: Route through the ERR family and the canonical ErrorCode registry rather than editing the fixture first. Determine whether claim-time scope expansion is still enforced under another code — ATM_CLAIM_FOREIGN_UNSTAGED_WIP is a candidate and is known to refuse a claim over unattributed dirty files — and if so, retire ATM_TASK_SCOPE_EXPANSION_REQUIRED properly and re-point the assertion. If no claim-time enforcement remains, decide whether the direction-lock and work-admission gates at edit and commit time are sufficient coverage, and record that decision; a new out-of-scope file that is staged before the claim is the case worth checking, since a guard keyed on modified-tracked files would not see it.
